$comment: The RFC 9728 section 5.1 / RFC 6750 section 3 challenge corpus (issue #127 criterion 3). Hand-maintained, and read by BOTH implementations: crates/ironauth-oidc/tests/protected_resource_metadata.rs and packages/ironauth-sdk/src/protected-resource.test.ts. Each side builds the challenge with its own builder and must produce `expected` byte for byte. Before this file the two sides asserted their own hardcoded strings, so 'the SDK matches the crate' was a claim no test could falsify.

cases.name: bare_401
cases.$why: A request with NO credential. RFC 6750 reserves the error parameters for a request that presented something, so the challenge carries only the pointer.

cases.name: invalid_token_401
cases.$why: A credential that was presented and failed. Both parameters travel, because `prm::challenge` writes `error_description` whenever it writes `error` while the SDK builder treats the description as optional. So a fixture omitting it could not be produced by both sides, and the agreeing case is the one that states it. The insufficient-scope builder below is a DIFFERENT function and pairs `error` with `scope` instead, which is why this sentence names `prm::challenge` rather than the crate.
cases.error_description: the access token is not valid for this resource
cases.expected: Bearer resource_metadata="https://api.example/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource/v1/mcp", error="invalid_token", error_description="the access token is not valid for this resource"

cases.name: insufficient_scope_403
cases.$why: The scope hint a client needs in order to ask for the right thing rather than guess. The pointer travels here too: a client may meet a 403 before it has ever seen a 401.
